did_you_know.text: Did you know? Ahab had seventy sons in Samaria, and they were in the care of the city officials and the tutors who raised them.
Did you know? Ahab’s seventy sons were killed by the people of the city, and their heads were sent to Jehu in Jezreel.
Did you know? Jehu presented the destruction of Ahab’s family as the fulfillment of the word of the LORD previously spoken through the prophet Elijah.
Did you know? On his way to Samaria, Jehu met the brothers of Ahaziah king of Judah, and the text states that there were forty-two of them.
Did you know? Jehu took Jehonadab son of Rechab with him after asking whether his heart was as fully committed to Jehu as Jehu’s was to him, and the two rode together in the chariot.
Did you know? Jehu announced that he intended to worship Baal more than Ahab had, but the text emphasizes that he said this deceptively in order to destroy Baal’s worshipers.
Did you know? Before striking down the worshipers of Baal, Jehu and Jehonadab son of Rechab made sure that no worshipers of the LORD were in the temple—only worshipers of Baal.
Did you know? Jehu stationed eighty men outside the temple of Baal and warned that anyone who allowed a worshiper of Baal to escape would pay with his life.

Did you know? Although Jehu did not wholeheartedly follow the law of the LORD, the LORD commended him for destroying Ahab’s family and promised that his descendants would sit on Israel’s throne to the fourth generation.

Did you know? Alongside the destruction of Baal worship, Jehu continued in the sins of Jeroboam and the worship of the golden calves at Bethel and Dan; during his reign, Hazael king of Aram began attacking Israel’s borders.
